# Topiqu — product and developer context

Topiqu is an AI content operations platform. It helps teams research, create, review, translate, publish, and improve business content. Its public website is https://topiqu.com and its application and API are hosted at https://app.topiqu.com.

## Product capabilities

- Knowledge base (beta, Pro and higher): notes, PDF/DOCX/TXT/Markdown files, web pages, whole sitemaps, Shopify catalogs and Heureka or Google Merchant product feeds become context for AI writing. Private sources are never cited publicly; only sources marked as public can become citations.
- AI writing with editorial review (Pro and higher): article formats (news, analysis, guide, comparison, opinion, story), live web research, a fact and copy review before publishing, and a fact-check panel that compares claims with sources.
- Article optimization score (all plans): deterministic checks for SEO, AI visibility, readability and trust, each with a concrete recommendation.
- Visibility (Premium and Custom): regular citation checks for selected questions in OpenAI answers, competitor detection, AI crawler and referral traffic, and article opportunities for uncited questions. Coverage is a sample, not a record of private conversations.
- Google Search Console (Premium and Custom): read-only access for article metrics, near-top and low-CTR opportunities, and an opt-in SEO autopilot limited to one article change per day with rollback.
- Languages: English, Czech, German and French for articles, translations, emails and the app interface. Translations can publish automatically or wait for human review; published translations get their own URLs and hreflang.
- Publishing: hosted publication on a topiqu.com subdomain or a custom domain (Pro and higher), publishing to Shopify blogs (installable from Shopify, with optional Shopify billing), per-channel controls for web, Shopify and LinkedIn, daily, weekly or irregular release scheduling, the Topiqu Sync WordPress plugin, External API v1, personal LinkedIn sharing, Google Analytics 4 and Google Ad Manager.
- Publication features: structured data, llms.txt, markdown versions of articles, answer boxes and FAQs, comments, reactions, polls, series and author pages.
- Media library with image provenance and publishing-rights tracking, a visual style editor (accent colours; gradients and custom fonts on Pro and higher), team members with scoped permissions, and several blogs per account.

## Plans

Prices are in USD per month. Every new blog starts with a 14-day trial with Premium features and 5 AI articles; no card is required to continue on Free.

- Free ($0): manual editor, free topiqu.com subdomain (up to three blogs), optimization score, media library, comments and basic analytics. No AI writing; Topiqu ads are shown on the blog.
- Pro ($49): 20 AI articles a month, knowledge base up to 50 sources, fact-check, translations, scheduling, custom domain, custom fonts and gradients, WordPress plugin, API and import. No Topiqu ads.
- Premium ($99): everything in Pro, 30 AI articles a month, citation tracking in OpenAI answers, Search Console insights and SEO autopilot, knowledge base up to 200 sources, reader sentiment analysis, priority indexing and priority support.
- Custom (on request): white-label, custom AI article allowance, knowledge base up to 500 sources, multiple brands and teams, apex domain setup, SLA.

Extra article packs (5, 12 or 25 articles) start at $8.99 and never expire. Translations, fact-checks, prompt improvements, sentiment analysis and Search Console suggestions do not use articles.

## External API v1

The Topiqu External API is a read-only REST API for retrieving content published for a Topiqu site. API v1 is a stable contract. Backwards-compatible fields and endpoints may be added without changing the versioned URL; breaking changes use a new major API version.

Base URL: `https://app.topiqu.com/api/v1`

Every request requires the API key belonging to the site whose articles are being retrieved:

```http
x-api-key: YOUR_API_KEY
```

Do not expose an API key in public browser code or commit it to source control. Use it from a server-side environment variable.

### First request

```bash
curl https://app.topiqu.com/api/v1/articles \
  -H "x-api-key: YOUR_API_KEY"
```

The API provides endpoints for listing published articles and retrieving an article by ID. Collection requests support `page`, `limit`, and `tag` query parameters. The default page size is 10 and the maximum is 100.

```http
GET /api/v1/articles?page=2&limit=25&tag=ai,marketing
```

Use HTTP status codes as the primary error signal. Treat human-readable error messages as diagnostic text. Clients should ignore unknown response fields so backwards-compatible additions do not break integrations.
